note: American Samoa, read in Title 41 (Immigration) of the American Samoa Code Annotated as the American Samoa Bar Association publishes it (asbar.org) on 2026-10-30. The Immigration Board may exclude anyone who isn't a national of the United States (or a spouse or child of an American Samoan) unless they show good character, a skill not readily available locally that is needed, a local sponsor and that they won't become a burden; everyone permitted to remain has a sponsor (an American Samoan, a US national or a firm doing business there), who answers for their costs, and may be sponsored for employment where the Board is satisfied of the need, within the yearly numerical limits; no alien may work without the Board's prior written approval (read as work for the sponsor). An alien is anyone who isn't a national or citizen of the United States, so US nationals and citizens need no permission (kept as free movement). Permanent resident status may be asked of the Attorney General after 20 continuous years of lawful presence (10 for a spouse of an American Samoan or US citizen), at most 50 a year on the 20-year ground (kept as the sponsored route's years to it). Fees, terms and decision times aren't in the sections read; naturalisation is the United States' and isn't read here.

sources.title: A.S.C.A. § 41.0401, Exclusion of persons not nationals of the United States
sources.said: The Immigration Board is authorized to exclude any person who does not qualify as a National of the United States, or as a spouse or child of an American Samoan, unless the person establishes to the satisfaction of the Board that: ... he offers a skill or expertise not readily available in the American Samoan community and the skill or expertise is needed in American Samoa;

sources.title: A.S.C.A. § 41.0408, Sponsors for persons permitted to remain
sources.said: Every person who applies for permission from the Board to remain in American Samoa is required to have a sponsor. ... Persons may be sponsored for purposes of other employment provided the Board is satisfied of the need and of the lack of permanent residents for such employment, and the person is within the numerical limitations established in chapter 03.

sources.title: A.S.C.A. § 41.0410, Employment of aliens-Penalty
sources.said: No alien may seek employment or become employed without prior written approval of the Board.

sources.title: A.S.C.A. § 41.0202, Definitions
sources.said: “Alien” means all persons who are not nationals or citizens of the United States of America.

sources.title: A.S.C.A. § 41.0403, Persons entitled to apply for permanent resident status
sources.said: any person who is physically and legally present in American Samoa for a continuous period of at least 20 years and of good moral character; ... The number of persons who may be granted the status of permanent resident in any fiscal year shall not exceed 50.
